```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.5,
  dev = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) "ragg_png" else "png")
```

The inference layers of inferplotR draw statistics, but they do not compute or
format them. Every estimate, interval, test statistic, p-value and adjustment
comes from `infercalcR::run_inference()` and `infercalcR::adjust_inference()`,
and every number in a label is a display string from
`infereportR::report_table()`. inferplotR chooses positions, draws the geometry
and keeps the complete result objects with the figure, so that they can be
inspected and reported.

```{r packages}
library(ggplot2)
library(inferplotR)
```

## Four layers

All four layers run per panel when the plot is built. Rows with non-finite x or
y are dropped first, as ggplot2 does for drawing.

### Means with confidence intervals

`stat_means()` draws the mean and its confidence interval for every x position.
The numbers are the estimate and interval of the one-sample t procedure
(`t_mean_one_sample`), used as an interval estimate, not as a test.

```{r means, fig.alt = "Dried plant weight for three groups: open circles for the plants and a point with a vertical line for each group mean and its 95% confidence interval."}
base <- ggplot(PlantGrowth, aes(group, weight)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1, position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  theme_figure() +
  labs(x = "Group", y = "Dried weight (g)")

base + stat_means(conf.level = 0.95)
```

### Pairwise comparisons

`stat_compare()` compares x groups pairwise with a named two-sample procedure,
adjusts the family of comparisons as declared and draws one bracket per pair.
For the pair `c(A, B)` the estimand is B minus A. With `reference`, every other
level is compared with that level; with `comparisons`, exactly the listed pairs;
with neither, all pairs in level order.

```{r compare, fig.alt = "The plant weights with two brackets above the groups, comparing each treatment with the control; each bracket is labeled with a Holm-adjusted p-value."}
base +
  stat_means() +
  stat_compare(method = "t_means_two_independent_welch", reference = "ctrl",
               adjust = "holm")
```

The label is the p-value by default. `label = "estimate_ci"` shows the
difference with its interval, `"estimate_ci_p"` both, and `"stars"` replaces
p-values below 0.05 with stars. A p-value of 0.05 or more keeps its display
string; it is never shown as "ns".

```{r compare-label, fig.width = 6, fig.alt = "The same comparison drawn for one explicit pair, labeled with the mean difference, its confidence interval and the p-value."}
base +
  stat_compare(method = "t_means_two_independent_welch",
               comparisons = list(c("trt1", "trt2")), adjust = "none",
               label = "estimate_ci_p")
```

The supported methods are `"t_means_two_independent_welch"`,
`"t_means_two_independent_student"`, `"rank_sum_mann_whitney"` and
`"brunner_munzel"`.

### Omnibus tests

`stat_omnibus()` runs one omnibus test per panel, with y as the outcome and the
x positions as groups, and writes the estimand, test statistic and p-value in
the top left corner. The methods are `"anova_one_way"`, `"anova_one_way_welch"`
and `"kruskal_wallis"`. Degrees of freedom are not part of the label, because
infereportR 0.1.0 has no display string for them; they are in the result.

```{r omnibus, fig.alt = "The plant weights with group means and a text label in the top left corner giving the F statistic and p-value of a one-way analysis of variance."}
base +
  stat_means() +
  stat_omnibus(method = "anova_one_way")
```

### Correlations

`stat_correlation()` runs one correlation per panel and labels the coefficient,
its interval and the p-value. The methods are `"correlation_pearson"`,
`"correlation_spearman"` and `"correlation_kendall"`. With `fit = TRUE` it also
draws the fitted mean line of infercalcR's linear prediction model
(`prediction_model_linear`) with its pointwise confidence band from
`infercalcR::predict_inference(interval = "mean")`, as dotted lines without fill.
The fit treats every row as an independent unit, and the line is never fitted
with `lm()` directly. With `fit = TRUE` the function returns two layers, which
`+` adds together.

```{r correlation, fig.alt = "Fuel economy against weight for 32 cars, with a solid fitted line, two dotted confidence lines and a label giving Pearson's r, its interval and the p-value."}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1) +
  stat_correlation(method = "correlation_pearson", fit = TRUE) +
  theme_figure() +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lb)", y = "Fuel economy (mpg)")
```

The label layers place their text at the panel edges (`-Inf` and `Inf`). Always
draw them together with a data layer, such as the points here, so that ggplot2
has data to train the position scales on.

## Explicit procedures and declared adjustments

The suite never chooses a procedure from the data. `stat_compare()`,
`stat_omnibus()` and `stat_correlation()` have no default method, so leaving it
out is an error when the layer is created:

```{r no-method}
res <- try(stat_compare(reference = "ctrl", adjust = "holm"), silent = TRUE)
cat(res)
```

With more than one comparison, the multiplicity adjustment must be declared;
`adjust = "none"` is allowed and documents the choice. With explicit
`comparisons`, the layer checks this when it is created:

```{r no-adjust-explicit}
res <- try(stat_compare(method = "t_means_two_independent_welch",
                        comparisons = list(c("ctrl", "trt1"), c("ctrl", "trt2"))),
           silent = TRUE)
cat(res)
```

With `reference` or all pairs, the number of comparisons is only known when the
plot is built. ggplot2 then reports "Problem while computing stat", with the
inferplotR condition as the cause:

```{r no-adjust-build}
p <- base + stat_compare(method = "t_means_two_independent_welch")
res <- try(ggplot_build(p), silent = TRUE)
cat(res)
```

The error conditions have classes such as `inferplotR_invalid_input`, so code can
catch them with `tryCatch()`.

## Facets: one analysis per panel

Every panel is its own analysis: `stat_means()` estimates per panel and x level,
`stat_compare()` forms one comparison family per panel, and `stat_omnibus()` and
`stat_correlation()` run once per panel. Here each supplement has its own Holm
family of three dose comparisons:

```{r facets, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.5, fig.alt = "Tooth length by vitamin C dose in two panels, orange juice and ascorbic acid; each panel shows means with intervals and three brackets with Holm-adjusted p-values."}
tooth <- ToothGrowth
tooth$dose <- factor(tooth$dose)
tooth$supp <- factor(tooth$supp, labels = c("Orange juice", "Ascorbic acid"))

facetted <- ggplot(tooth, aes(dose, len)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1, position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  stat_means() +
  stat_compare(method = "t_means_two_independent_welch", adjust = "holm") +
  facet_wrap(~supp) +
  theme_figure() +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg/day)", y = "Tooth length (mm)")
facetted
```

## The results behind the figure

`inference_results()` builds the plot once and returns every infercalcR result
its layers computed, named by layer, method and panel:

```{r results}
results <- inference_results(facetted)
names(results)
```

These are ordinary infercalcR result objects. infercalcR and infereportR read
them as they would read any other result, for example as a sentence for the
manuscript:

```{r report-text}
oj <- results[["inferplotR:compare:t_means_two_independent_welch:panel1"]]
infercalcR::result_data(oj)[, c("row_id", "estimate", "p.value", "p.adjusted")]
cat(infereportR::report_text(oj, p = "adjusted"), sep = "\n\n")
```

## One table: `figure_report()`

`figure_report()` passes every result through `infereportR::report_table()` and
binds the rows, with the layer and panel each one came from. By default
(`p = "auto"`) it reports adjusted p-values where a result has an adjustment and
raw ones elsewhere.

```{r figure-report}
tab <- figure_report(facetted)
tab[tab$figure_layer == 3, c("figure_panel", "contrast", "estimate_display",
                             "interval_display", "p_display")]
```

## The `inferplot()` bundle

`inferplot()` adds the theme, the black-and-white scales, the raw observations,
the means and the tests you name, in one call. It adds no test unless its
procedure is named:

```{r bundle, fig.alt = "Plant weights with means, a one-way analysis of variance label and two Holm-adjusted comparisons with the control."}
bundle <- ggplot(PlantGrowth, aes(group, weight)) +
  inferplot(compare = "t_means_two_independent_welch", reference = "ctrl",
            adjust = "holm", omnibus = "anova_one_way") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Group", y = "Dried weight (g)")
bundle
```

The omnibus label sits at the top edge of the panel and the brackets are
stacked up to that edge, so the extra expansion at the top of the y scale leaves
room for the label above the brackets.

## Precomputed results with `infereportR::stat_inference()`

Results computed elsewhere can be drawn on an inferplotR figure with
`infereportR::stat_inference()`, which takes a finished result and explicit
bracket positions. Here infercalcR runs a Brunner-Munzel test of `trt2` against
`trt1`:

```{r precomputed, fig.alt = "Plant weights with means and one bracket between the two treatment groups, labeled with the p-value of a Brunner-Munzel test computed before plotting."}
pg <- PlantGrowth
bm <- infercalcR::run_inference(
  infercalcR::method_spec("brunner_munzel"),
  x = pg$weight[pg$group == "trt2"], y = pg$weight[pg$group == "trt1"],
  result_id = "bm-trt2-trt1")
row_id <- infercalcR::result_data(bm)$row_id
positions <- data.frame(row_id = row_id, group1 = "trt1", group2 = "trt2",
                        y_position = 6.6)

base +
  stat_means() +
  infereportR::stat_inference(bm, positions, groups = levels(pg$group),
                              text_size = 9 / .pt)
```

The precomputed result is not part of `inference_results()`, which returns only
what the inferplotR layers computed.

## Sources

The calculations are those of infercalcR and the display strings those of
infereportR (Heller, <https://github.com/CTTIR/infercalcR>,
<https://github.com/CTTIR/infereportR>). The ggproto objects follow the public
ggplot2 extension guide, `vignette("extending-ggplot2", package = "ggplot2")`.
See the README for the full list of sources.
